blocks.text: Condo buildings in Mission West

Geography: Mission West is inside the City of Mission, on the western side of the city, covering Silverdale and the rural fringe toward Stave Falls and Ruskin. City of Mission planning, zoning and the flat 10% tax penalty are the frame throughout, and the FVRD rural 5% + 5% regime does not apply here. Sources differ on the classification of Archer Green: a presale directory lists its ownership as "Condominium" while its building type is "Townhouse," and MLS® listings for the same complex record Sub-Type Townhouse with Ownership Type Freehold Strata. The Wilson Street parks are labelled "Mission-West" on the mission-west and mission-mobile-homes feeds and "Stave Falls" on the stave-falls feed, for the same Wilson Street addresses. The label does not change the parks' tenure or the City tax frame.
Streets, schools and getting around Mission West

items.t: Every first-page card is labelled board sub-area "Mission-West" with a "Mission" mailing address, on streets including Wilson Street, Hayward Street, Olson Avenue, Haffner Terrace, Silverdale Avenue, Keystone Avenue, Gunn Avenue, Nelson Street and Townshipline Avenue.

Board geography: "Mission West" is one of nine sub-areas of the Fraser Valley board community "Mission" (Dewdney Deroche, Durieu, Hatzic, Hemlock, Lake Errock, Mission, Mission West, Stave Falls, Steelhead).
The attached row recorded no Mission West sales, so no attached ratio or attached price statement exists for this sub-area.

The defining plan area on this ground is Silverdale: the Silverdale Comprehensive Planning Area (SCPA) is a 3,440-acre area, sometimes known as Southwest Mission, defined in the City's Official Community Plan and designated for urban growth, with a Central Neighbourhood Plan process and a Master Infrastructure Strategy underway. Development timing, densities and population claims for individual Silverdale listings in feed text are listing copy only: Not verified as facts for any specific parcel.

The City's Rural Mission Strategy also covers this side of the city — the City describes it as covering the City's rural communities "From Stave Falls, Steelhead and Silverdale to our other rural neighbourhoods," building on the Official Community Plan. Silverdale is therefore both an urban-growth planning area and, in the City's rural strategy, a rural neighbourhood — the two descriptions are the City's own, for different purposes.

Health care: Mission Memorial Hospital, 7324 Hurd Street, consists of a 25-bed medical inpatient unit, a 20-bed PATH unit and a 10-bed Christine Morrison Hospice, and provides primary acute care, outpatient and inpatient, general medicine, laboratory and diagnostic services.

Servicing (City water/sewer vs well/septic) for Mission West acreage lots: Not verified at parcel level — feed listing text repeatedly references wells, septic systems and community water/septic in the Wilson Street parks, which is listing copy only. Silvermere Lake shoreline: any specific property's dock, moorage, shoreline-tenure or water-access rights: Not verified — no official source confirms them for a Mission West parcel.

items.t: Secondary suites (City frame): all secondary suites in Mission must be registered with the City; a suite is a self-contained living space in a single family home forming part of the same real estate entity, suites are not permitted in townhouses or rowhomes, a new suite goes through the building permit process, and an annual secondary suite fee of $63 plus applicable utility user fees is applied to the property tax notice. The in-house size cap, any owner-occupancy rule and the exact parking count: Not verified pass.

Manufactured-home pad rent (MHPTA), for the Wilson Street park homes excluded in: pad-rent increases are capped at 2.3% plus a proportional amount for 2026, and 2.2% plus a proportional amount for 2027.

blocks.text: Good to know about Mission West

items.t: Silverdale is planned twice, in two different City documents. It is the 3,440-acre Comprehensive Planning Area designated for urban growth and, at the same time, one of the rural communities named in the City's Rural Mission Strategy. A listing that quotes only the growth story — or only the rural story — is quoting half the City's own framing.

Archer Green's unit numbers are not a unit count. Listings show unit numbers into the 150s at 8335 Nelson Street, but no source checked states the complex's total — a buyer (or a page) that turns the highest unit number into a count is inventing a figure. Total: Not confirmed.

The two Wilson Street parks pull in opposite directions from a seniors expectation, and they hide under two board labels. Ruskin Place markets itself as family-friendly with no age restrictions; Triple Creek Estates lists a playground and no pet restrictions with no age rule stated. Search both "Mission West" and "Stave Falls" for Wilson Street homes or listings will be missed — the same addresses carry both labels on different feeds.
Mission West's "highest ratio in Mission" is one sale. It is a thin-shelf signal, not a ranking to build pricing on.

A detached second home on a rural Mission West lot usually starts as a zoning question, not a permit. An in-house secondary suite must be registered with the City (building permit for a new suite; $63 annual suite fee plus utility fees; no suites in townhouses), while a detached coach home or garden cottage is a separate accessory-dwelling question governed by the parcel's zone — and on ALR land the ALC frame caps the second residence at 90 m² or 186 m² by parcel size.

items.t: Official Community Plan: Bylaw 6405-2026, adopted June 1, 2026, replacing and repealing OCP Bylaw 6350-2025. The Silverdale Comprehensive Planning Area is a 3,440-acre area, sometimes known as Southwest Mission, defined in the OCP and designated for urban growth, with a Central Neighbourhood Plan process and a Master Infrastructure Strategy underway; the City's Rural Mission Strategy also covers this side of the city ("From Stave Falls, Steelhead and Silverdale to our other rural neighbourhoods"). Development timing, densities and population claims for individual Silverdale listings in feed text are listing copy only: Not verified as facts for any specific parcel. Mission's Lougheed Highway Corridor Plan is in preparation, not adopted — Council endorsed Focused Land Use Option #2 on July 20, 2026; no corridor-plan adoption is claimed for the Highway 7 corridor serving this side of the city.

ALR: any Mission West parcel in the Agricultural Land Reserve follows the ALC housing frame — one principal residence at a maximum of 500 m², a suite within the principal only, plus at most one additional residence of 90 m² (parcels ≤40 ha) or 186 m² (parcels >40 ha) — and ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)) ( Whether a specific parcel is in the ALR: Not verified at parcel level. BC Assessment farm thresholds, where they apply, run in the full three-tier form ($2,500 at 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 plus 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by October 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an error.

Servicing and shoreline: servicing (City water/sewer vs well/septic) for Mission West acreage lots is not verified at parcel level — feed text referencing wells, septic systems and community water/septic in the Wilson Street parks is listing copy only. blocks.text: Mission West Condos and Townhomes: streets and boundaries

items.t: Mission West is a board sub-area for the western side of the City of Mission: the Silverdale area and the rural fringe toward Stave Falls and Ruskin, on streets including Silverdale Avenue, Gunn Avenue, Nelson Street and Townshipline Avenue, all inside the City of Mission.

The City's own name for the growth ground is the Silverdale Comprehensive Planning Area (SCPA), a 3,440-acre area sometimes known as Southwest Mission, designated in the Official Community Plan for urban growth.

The SCPA is bordered by Silverdale Creek to the east, rural, agricultural and Kwantlen First Nations lands to the north, Silvermere Lake to the west and the Fraser River and Agricultural Land Reserve lands to the south.

blocks.text: Mission West Condos and Townhomes: the housing stock

items.t: The plan sequence is the housing fact: the City's Silverdale terms of reference state neighbourhood plans are required for areas anticipating growth in density, following a collaborative planning process with technical due diligence and full cost accounting, before subdivision and development proceed under the plan.
The existing stock the plan will sit beside is rural: the City's Rural Mission Strategy covers the City's rural communities, naming Silverdale among them, building on the new Official Community Plan.

blocks.text: Mission West Condos and Townhomes: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Rainwater rules are written before the homes are: the Silverdale Central Neighbourhood Plan's Integrated Rainwater Management Plan applies the City's Development and Subdivision Control Bylaw 5650-2017 goals, including drainage protection for life, livelihood and property and control of surface ponding.

blocks.text: Mission West Condos and Townhomes: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Silverdale Elementary, 29715 Donatelli Avenue, is one of only three elementary schools the district's facilities plan identifies as serving Mission's rural areas, alongside Dewdney and Deroche elementaries in the east.
Mission Senior Secondary, 32939 7th Avenue, is the district's single Grades 10 to 12 school, so every Mission West student travels east across the city for senior secondary.

The West Coast Express timetable effective January 5, 2026 runs five weekday trains from Mission City Station between 5:25 and 7:25 a.m., arriving at Waterfront Station 75 minutes later, with no weekend or statutory holiday service; station-to-door times for Mission West addresses are not stated by any official source.
Homes outside Mission's waste collection area pay a $36.00 rural recycling fee on the tax notice instead of the garbage and recycling charges, $62.28 with a secondary dwelling.

blocks.text: Mission West Condos and Townhomes: development and new projects

items.t: Silverdale Central Neighbourhood Plan (CNP), Silverdale: the neighbourhood plan for the central part of the 3,440-acre Silverdale Comprehensive Planning Area, with a Master Infrastructure Strategy underway and an Integrated Rainwater Management Plan dated May 31, 2024 prepared for the plan by Silverdale Hills GP Inc. Status: neighbourhood plan and infrastructure planning underway, City plans material (as of November 3, 2026).

Silverdale West and East neighbourhood plans: not yet open for initiation — the City's terms of reference gate them behind 65% of the Central Neighbourhood Plan's South Slopes being under application or engineering services committed. Status: gated, not initiated (as of November 3, 2026).

blocks.text: Mission West Condos and Townhomes: costs and taxes

items.t: The Mission West utility difference is the rural edge: a serviced single family home paid $1,892.28 in 2026 flat-rate utilities, while a home outside the waste collection area pays only the $36.00 rural recycling fee for the waste side, so two Mission West properties can carry very different tax-notice utility lines depending on where services reach.

blocks.text: Mission West Condos and Townhomes: getting around

items.t: BC Transit route 32 West Heights is the west-side route, and route 31 Valley Connector links Mission to Abbotsford via the Abbotsford–Mission Highway.

Mission City Station, 33200 North Railway Avenue, is the West Coast Express terminus, on the opposite side of the city from Silverdale; limited weekday TransLink 701 bus service also runs to and from the station.

blocks.text: Mission West Condos and Townhomes: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check rainwater and drainage designations before assuming a lot is buildable as shown: the Central Neighbourhood Plan's map layers include watercourses, biophysical constraints, designated environmentally sensitive areas and flood construction levels.
